cases.narrative:
On 10/25/1981, hunters discovered her partial remains in Pocatello, ID - scattered bones and deteriorated clothing matching that of what she was wearing. They also found some partial remains belonging to Tina Anderson. Tina was identified soon later via dental records, but the remains thought to be Patricia's couldn't be positively identified. In 2007, Patricia's remains, which had been misplaced by police and then relocated, were identified via DNA.

Then in In October 1986, a hunter in Two Mile Canyon, outside Malad, Idaho discovered a partial human skull. They named her "Oneida Jane Doe" and 2022, Othram Inc. announced they had identified her skull.

cases.name: Vicki Jo Quinn
cases.about: She was a student at Pocatello High School.
cases.narrative:
On 4/21/1962, a horseback posse found her shoes. A grave was found nearby which contained her body, clothed in panties and a bra, was found in a shallow grave hidden by branches on the Fort Hall Indian Reservation 10 miles north of Pocatello, ID. Larsen had stabbed approximately 30 times and had superficial throat wounds. Burt was involved in digging her grave and helping to bury her.

Witness Diane Oney, 15 said she and Vicki Jo met them at a teenage dance and went for a ride with the boys and she and Burt stayed in the car while Vicki Jo and Larsen went for a walk. Larsen returned to the car alone, claiming Vicki Jo had decided to walk home. Larsen took Burt and showed him Vicki Jo's body and they both dragged her to the grave, took Diane home and returned to cover the grave.

cases.name: Jennifer “Jenn” Diane Stephens Leigh
cases.about: Her obituary said, "She is remembered by her loved ones as a feisty and clever girl who knew exactly what she wanted. One could not tell her there was something she could not do. Jenn and her cousin, Erin, may have been the slyest of all the cousins. Jenn was their protector on many occasions and she always had the biggest heart for her family. Growing up, Jenn attended several different schools in Idaho and Utah while moving around with her family. She was a student at Skyline Senior High School and later went on to earn her General Educational Development certificate. On July 22nd, 1997, Jenn welcomed her first born Nataiela Maree Croft with Will Shomaker. She was blessed to give birth to her second daughter Roxanne Lynn Lott on January 26th, 2009 with Troy Lott. On April 4th, 2013, Jenn married Jesse Leigh with whom she gave birth to her youngest child Blake Steven Leigh on December 12th later that year. Jenn loved her children more than anything and she loved being a mother. She could not wait to become a grandma. For 22 years, Jenn established a career as a professional cook. It was a dream of hers to own a restaurant so she could share her incredible skills with her friends, family and community. She was lucky enough to practice her craft for many years at ButterBurr’s Restaurant in Pocatello, Idaho. As a front-runner in opening ButterBurr’s second location Lickety Split, Jenn was able to see a piece of her dream come to life. It was because of this and many other accomplishments Jenn made throughout her career; her family was so proud of what she put into it. Jenn was always a hard worker and found passion in many things she did. She will be remembered as a great listener and problem solver. Seeing anyone who was feeling down brought out her nurturing side, she would always give the best hugs then try to lighten the mood with her creative silliness and laughter. Jenn loved spending time outdoors and she especially enjoyed boating and camping. She carried an old soul and was an avid music listener. She absolutely loved Rock n’ Roll, R&B and Rap music enjoying artists such as Tool, Korn, The Offspring, Fleetwood Mac, Eminem, Dr. Dre and Bone Thugs N’ Harmony. She was more adventurous than most. One of her favorite pastimes was going to concerts where she loved to sing and dance her heart out."
